elements.content: Communication Goal: I can say who I am, where I come from and how I am.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 1. Hello there!
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Pronouns + to be (Where are you from?)
- Materials: World map, flag cards, pronoun cards, COSYmanuals 'to be' and 'pronouns' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• use subject pronouns I, you, he, she, it, we, they
• form positive and negative sentences with the verb to be
• ask and answer 'Where are you from?'
Recycling & Course Continuity:

Prior learning: Recycles greetings and names from Lesson 1.

Next lesson: Lesson 3 recycles 'to be' to describe people with adjectives.
Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

i — the pronoun for yourself. Example: I am from Egypt.
you — the person or people you speak to. Example: You are my friend.
he — a male person. Example: He is my brother.
she — a female person. Example: She is my sister.
it — a thing or animal. Example: It is a big city.
we — you and I, or a group including me. Example: We are students.
they — other people or things. Example: They are teachers.
am — the 'be' form for I. Example: I am happy.
is — the 'be' form for he, she, it. Example: She is tired.
are — the 'be' form for you, we, they. Example: They are here.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Where are you from? (asking about origin)
• I am from... (stating your origin)
• He / She is from... (stating another person's origin)
• We are students. (stating identity)
• I am not from... (negative origin statement)
• Are you from...? (yes/no question about origin)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'the pronoun for yourself'?
Which word means 'the person or people you speak to'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Short forms of 'to be' and question intonation

I'm /aɪm/ — contraction of I am
you're /jɔː/ — contraction of you are
he's /hiːz/ — contraction of he is
aren't /ɑːnt/ — contraction of are not
Listen and repeat:
I'm from Egypt. She's from Spain. Are you from Italy?

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'be' to say who someone is, how they feel, and where they are from.

Form:
The verb 'to be': I am / You are / He, she, it is / We are / They are. Negative: I'm not, isn't, aren't. Question: Am I...? Are you...? Is he...?

Examples:
• I am a student.
• She is from Spain.
• We are happy today.
• They are not teachers.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
My name ___ Alex.
They ___ from Italy.
I ___ tired today.
She ___ not a teacher.
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I am ... (a student / happy / from Egypt).
• She is ... (a teacher / tired / from Spain).
• They are ... (students / at home / happy).
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• Are you a student? — Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
• Is she from France? — Yes, she is. / No, she isn't.
• Are they happy? — Yes, they are. / No, they aren't.
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write two true sentences with 'I am...' and 'I am not...'.
• Introduce two people in the class with 'He/She is...'.
Reading: Pronouns + to be (Where are you from?)

I am Alex and I am from Egypt. You are Sam and you are from England. He is Omar and he is from Morocco. She is Maria and she is from Spain. We are all students in the same class. They are our teachers. We are happy to learn English together.
Where is Alex from?
Who is from Spain?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: Hello. Where are you from?
B: I'm from Italy. And you?
A: I'm from Egypt. Are you a student?
B: Yes, I am. We are in the same class.
A: Great! Is she from Spain?
B: No, she isn't. She's from France.
Where is the second speaker from?
Is the woman from Spain?
Speaking task: Ask your partner where they are from and where two family members are from. Use 'he/she is from...'.

• Where are you from?
• Where is your best friend from?
• Are you a student or a worker?
• Is your teacher from your city?
• Why are you learning English?
Role-play: You are at an international student meeting. Introduce yourself, say where you are from, and ask three people the same questions.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about you and your family using 'am/is/are'.
Model: I am from ... My mother is from ... My father is ... We are ... They are ...
